 :J U D G M E N T:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of 20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 18.08.2022 at about 9.35 a.m., when the Petitioner was proceeding in Honda Activa Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA- 04-HP-8930 and when she reached near Shettihalli - Mallasandra main road, Shettihalli Junction, Bengaluru, at SCCH 15 3 MVC No.4642/2022 that time, one Tata Mini Goods Tanker vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AE-0438 driven by its driver came in a rash and negligent manner and with high speed and dashed against the Petitioner's motor vehicle.

As a result,
the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries to all over the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Eskay Health Care Hospital,
Bengaluru, wherein the Petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.

She had spent Rs.3,00,000/-
amount towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges etc.,
4.
Prior to the date of accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and she was working as a Tailor and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
The said accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tata Mini Goods Tanker vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AE-0438 by its driver.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and SCCH 15 4 MVC No.4642/2022 severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, the Respondent No.1 remained absent and he was placed exparte.
The Respondent No.2 had appeared before the Court through its Counsel and filed its Objection statement to the main Petition.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and the expenses incurred for the treatment.
Further it contended that as on the date of accident, the offending vehicle was not insured with the Respondent No.2.
Further it contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective driving license at the time of accident.
Further it contended that said offending vehicle being a commercial vehicle the same was plied on road, SCCH 15 5 MVC No.4642/2022 without valid permit, Authorization and Fitness of the said vehicle.
The said accident occurred due to the negligence of the Petitioner only.

Therefore, it is not liable to pay the compensation to the Taradevi M.T. Alias Tara vs Miracle Agro Products Pvt Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155599309/
2 Petitioner.

sentences.text: On these grounds it has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.
6. On the rival Pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1. Whether the Petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 18.08.2022 at about 9.35 a.m., on Shettihalli - Mallasandra main road, Shettihalli Junction, Bengaluru City, due to the rash and negligent driving of the Tata Mini Goods Tanker vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AE-0438 by its driver?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
3. What Order or Award?
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-13.
Further, she examined two witnesses as PW.2 & 3 and got marked 6 documents at Ex.14 to 19 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order,
 for the following :
 REASONS 9. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that, she had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tata Mini Goods Tanker vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-AE-0438 by its driver.
SCCH 15 7 MVC No.4642/2022 10.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tata Mini Goods Tanker vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 01-AE-0438 by its driver.

sentences.text: In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and got marked 13 documents at Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-13 and she has re-iterated the Petition averments in her Chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 to Ex.P-11 are the True copies of FIR, Complaint, Spot mahazar with Spot Sketch, Police Notice and Reply, IMV report, Wound Certificate, Charge sheet, Discharge summary,
Medical bills, X-rays, Aadhaar card and DL.
12.

Upon going through the documents exhibited, Ex.P- 1 & 2 are the True copies of the FIR &
Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by Petitioner herself, the Peenya Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the offending Tata Mini Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AE- 0438 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of SCCH 15 8 MVC No.4642/2022 IPC.
Ex.P.3 is the true copy of Spot Mahazar with Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and Sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P4 & 5 are the Notice with Reply.
Ex.P.6 is the IMV report which shows that the said accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.

Ex.P.7 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows the following injuries:-
1) Lacerated wound at postrial medial aspect left lower limb and compound fracture of tibia and fibula
As per the opinion of the Doctor, said injury is grievous in nature.

Ex.P.8 is the True copy of the Charge sheet which has been submitted by the Sub Inspector of Police, Peenya Traffic Police Station against the driver of the offending Tata Mini Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AE-0438 for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of IPC.
Ex.P.9 is the Discharge summary of the Petitioner.
Ex.P10 is the Medical bills.
Ex.P11 is the X-rays.
Ex.P12 is the Aadhaar card and Ex.P13 is the DL.

Further, the Petitioner has examined Doctor SCCH 15 9 MVC No.4642/2022 by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P.14 and 15 and also examined Medical Record Technician by name Madhusudan C.H as PW.3 and got marked 4 documents at Ex.P16 to 19.
13.
PW.1 is subjected for cross examination by the learned counsel for the Respondent No.2.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the testimony of PW.1.
Further, the Respondent No.2 did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.
Hence, the Respondent No.2 has failed to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the Petitioner has proved the rash and negligent driving of the offending Tata Mini Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AE-0438 by its driver and due to the said accident, she had sustained grievous injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.

SCCH 15 10 MVC No.4642/2022 14. Issue No.2: As the Petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Goods vehicle by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.

sentences.text: In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown her age as 39 years.
The Petitioner has produced the Aadhaar card and DL at Ex.P12 & 13, which shows her date of birth as 13.11.1984.
The accident has taken place on 18.08.2022.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the Petitioner was 37 years, 9 months and 05 days.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 38 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
16. Further, the Petitioner has averred that, she was working as a Tailor and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, she has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.15,500/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads:
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING :
18.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P-7 issued by the Medical Officer of the Eskay hospital, Bengaluru shows that in the said accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries i.e.,
1) Lacerated wound at Postrial medial aspect left lower limb and compound fracture of tibia and fibula
As per the opinion of the Doctor, said injury is grievous in nature.

19. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding SCCH 15 12 MVC No.4642/2022 compensation of 30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
II.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
20. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of 15,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID-UP PERIOD:
21.

The Petitioner deposed in her evidence that she had taken treatment at Eskay hospital,
Bengaluru.
Upon going through Ex.P.9 - Discharge Summary shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient in the said hospital from 18.08.2022 to 22.08.2022.
Therefore, while calculating the total period of which the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient, it comes to 05 days.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation Taradevi M.T. Alias Tara vs Miracle Agro Products Pvt Ltd on 4 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155599309/
5 of 31,000/- under this head (@ 15,500/- per month ).
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
23.

sentences.text: Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also she might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for her conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of 6,000/- (@ 100/- per day) towards attendants charges, 6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and 6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 18,000/- under this head.

SCCH 15 14 MVC No.4642/2022 V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
24.

entities.text: MVC No.4642/2022 V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The petitioner has stated in her evidence that, she had spent Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical and other incidental charges.
In order to prove this fact, she has produced medical bills at Ex.P.10.
In the cross-examination PW.1 admitted that Rs.80,000/- was reimbursed by the insurance and she had spent Rs.22,818/- for medical expenses.
I have gone through the medical bills produced by the PW.1.

The bill at Sl.No.1 is Xerox copy, wherein seal and signature was made and the said document clearly shows the total amount is Rs.1,06,583/- and approval amount is Rs.80,430/- and discount Rs.26,153/- and received amount is Rs.24,153/-.
I have gone through the entire medical bills and the acceptable medical bills comes at Rs.26,818/-.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the same to be taken at 26,900/-.
Hence, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner is entitled for 26,900/- under this head.
SCCH 15 15 MVC No.4642/2022 VI.
COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS / COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY:
25. The petitioner has stated that due to the injuries sustained by her in the accident, she has suffered permanent disablement and she is not able to do her work as she used to do earlier.
Even in her evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.

26. Further, the Petitioner got examined one witness by name Dr. Nagaraj B.N as P.W.2 who has deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a Road Traffic Accident and the treatment taken by her.
Further, he assessed the physical disability of the Petitioner towards left lower limb at 35% and whole body disability at 12%.
PW.2 got marked Clinical Notes and X-ray at Ex.P14 and 15
. In the cross- examination, PW.2 has deposed that he has not personally treated the Petitioner and he has not seen the further treatment medical records of the Petitioner.

He further SCCH 15 16 MVC No.4642/2022 admitted that the fracture of the Petitioner is united and the Petitioner has not taken any treatment for the problem which he mentioned in the Para No.5 of his chief-affidavit.
He denied the other suggestions.

Having regard to the medical records placed on record, the evidence of P.W.2 and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 5% would be just and proper.

sentences.text: As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 15.

With multiplier of 15, income of 15,500/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to her whole body at 5%, the loss of future income comes to 1,39,500/- (15,500/- x 12 = 1,86,000/-,
1,86,000/-x 15 x 5/100 = 1,39,500/-).

Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of 1,39,500/- under this head.
SCCH 15 17 MVC No.4642/2022 TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
28.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering  30,000/-
2. Loss of amenities  15,000/-
3. Loss of income during the laid up  31,000/-
period 4.

Attendant's charges, Extra diet,  18,000/-
and conveyance 5.

Medical expenses  26,900/-
6. Loss of Future Income  1,39,500/ Total 2,60,400/-
29.
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of 2,60,400/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.
30. Regarding Liability:

This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash SCCH 15 18 MVC No.4642/2022 and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Offending Tata Mini Goods vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AE-0438.
There is no dispute about the validity of the Policy at the time of the accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to satisfy the award amount.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1, has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.

Accordingly,
I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Partly in the Affirmative".
31. Issue No.3

: In view of my findings on Issues No. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the U/S 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioner.
